messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran the coverage scan against our audit-event catalog. Large gaps across API gateway, auth (session, RBAC), console UI, billing service webhooks, and runtime (kms/key-ops). Need to triage backlog + decide schema changes for customer-facing events. Suggest quick sync + owner assignments.

sam: tl;dr where are the biggest risks? is this blocking SOC request?

maya: biggest risk = missing principal and resource fields in gateway logs for failed token exchanges, and no kms_key_id in runtime encryption ops. SOC wants proof of customer-visible events for billing adjustments.

eli: can you paste failing examples?

maya: pasted below:
```json
{
  "event_type": "auth_failure",
  "service": "api-gateway",
  "details": "token denied",
  "timestamp": "..."
}
```
Missing: principal.id, principal.type, resource.path, request_id, iam_action, and audit.schema_version.

jonah: oof. For RBAC changes we also need ROLE_ASSIGN/ROLE_REVOKE events with before/after snapshots. Right now console only logs role name change but no actor.

priya: KMS note: when runtime rotates keys we write to ops log but not customer audit. Customers expect kms_key_id + encrypted_key_version in audit stream. Also ensure we don't leak full key material.

audit-bot: scan complete — 27 service gaps found. Summary: gateway(6), auth(5), console(4), billing(7), runtime(5). See https://go/reports/audit-scan-196345 for details :eyes:

sam: propose short-term: (A) add request_id & principal.* to gateway sync layer (B) console: add actor + role delta for RBAC flows (C) billing: emit adjustment events with invoice_id + delta (D) runtime: include kms_key_id + op_type. Estimate: 3 devs, 2 sprints.

maya: +1. We should also surface schema changes to customers via changelog + versioned schema (audit.schema_version). Avoid breaking consumers.

eli: who picks up drafting the schema? I can start a strawman PR for v2 of audit schema. Will include sample events & validator.

maya: assign eli for schema PR (RDW-2821). assign sam to gateway changes (RDW-2822). assign priya to KMS runtime work (RDW-2823). jonah please handle console RBAC events (RDW-2824). I'll own backlog triage & release notes (RDW-2825).

jonah: ack. quick Q — do we want to buffer old consumers with a transformer in the console to output legacy fields for 2 releases?

maya: yes, add a compatibility flag and deprecation timeline in the spec. e.g., support legacy.event_principal until 2026-12-31.

priya: security concern: ensure KMS id is hashed/pseudonymized for customer-facing events? Some customers saw raw key ids as sensitive.

sam: prefer storing kms_key_id in event as ID (not secret) but avoid key material. Add access control to audit export endpoints.

maya: action items:
- eli: draft schema PR + JSON schema validator + examples (RDW-2821)
- sam: gateway request principal + request_id (RDW-2822)
- priya: runtime KMS event + pseudonymization guidance (RDW-2823)
- jonah: console RBAC role delta events + compatibility transformer (RDW-2824)
- maya: release notes + customer disclosure plan + backlog grooming (RDW-2825)

sam: I'll aim to have a prototype in 3 days. @maya please coordinate with support for any incoming tickets.

maya: will do. Let's sync Friday 11am PT. Adding a calendar invite.

audit-bot: calendar invite created by maya — Audit coverage triage — Fri 11:00 PT

eli: one more ask — add automated validation in CI that rejects events not matching audit.schema_version or missing required fields.

maya: good call. add to RDW-2821 spec.

jonah: leaving notes in the RDW Epic: https://go/epic/audit-coverage (comments with sample events)

priya: flagged privacy review for KMS pseudonymization — ticket RDW-2826

maya: thanks all. closing thread; will follow up with PR links in channel. :thumbsup:
